title: Qualify readable work through real page and payload boundaries
trigger: Lab work reader pagination payloadRef missing summary incomplete coverage interleaved current preview audit
guidance: When projecting readable work from retained traces, qualify three independent coordinates: the retained page cursor, availability of separately stored payloads, and latest observed activity within stable reading order. A nonzero cursor means a page was consumed, not that the reader should restart. Complete sequence coverage does not imply complete payload coverage. Use explicit turn-scoped reads, retryable failures and the existing bounded display cache; preserve raw envelopes and never parse retention previews as evidence. Keep unresolved or retention-lost payloads visible. Select the current excerpt by latest update sequence while retaining original block order for reading. Browser fixtures must honor actual page limits, payload references and failed-read behavior; returning every event for every request can conceal a broken reader even when reducer tests pass.

evidence.note: Corrects the three final-audit Lab findings without changing core/client source, provider requests, raw storage or the frozen 3217c8d package pair. Large payloads are read explicitly through existing scope checks and the shared eight-payload cache.

All three browser regressions fail on d62cc26 and pass after correction: interleaved preview, 205-record three-page progression, separate 60k-character payloads with failed-read retry and per-event loss disclosure.46 UI/Markdown checks and both prior intercepted Edge reading/Markdown journeys pass. No live provider, running user service or installed-host proof.

recheck: Recheck cursor transitions, payload cache eviction/scope, retention envelopes and source ordering if the raw trace store or reader changes. This qualifies a bounded loaded-window reader, not durable semantic-block pagination or unlimited retention.
